issues.failure_explanation: The stated limit is false. Counterexample from the paper's own identities: take $\beta\equiv 1$, $\psi\equiv 0$ on the unit disc; then the double-layer potential equals $\int_{\partial\Omega}\partial\Phi(x,y)/\partial n_y\,d\sigma_y = 1$ for all interior $x$, so $u\equiv 1$ and the left side is $1$, while the right side is $u(x^*)-\frac12\beta(x^*) = 1-\frac12 = \frac12$. The correct relation is $\lim = \int_{\partial\Omega}\beta(y)\frac{\partial\Phi(x^*,y)}{\partial n_y}d\sigma_y + \frac12\beta(x^*) = u(x^*)-\int_\Omega\Phi(x^*,y)\psi(y)dy$. The mechanism is 'other' because the theorem is quoted without proof and simply asserts a false identity: there is no proof inference to fail, no invoked dependency, and no argument establishing a weaker conclusion.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition hypothesizes only non-expansiveness, defined in the paper's Fredholm NN definition as $q\le 1$, but its bound contains the factor $e^{1-q}/(1-q)$, which is undefined at $q=1$ (and the rate $e^{-(1-q)v_M}$ degenerates to 1, i.e., no decay). For the Poisson BIE on the unit disc — the paper's first main example — the kernel is the constant $1/(4\pi)$, so the BIE map is $\beta\mapsto 2(f-N)-\frac{1}{2\pi}\int_0^{2\pi}\beta\,d\theta$, whose norm on $C(\partial\Omega)$ is exactly $1$ (attained on constants); the optimal non-expansiveness constant is $q=1$ and no $q<1$ is admissible. Hence the quoted FNN error bound does not apply to the Poisson case, so the 'explicit error bounds' asserted via Theorem error-bounds-thrm's final clause and used to explain the Poisson experiments in Section 6.1.4 (and claimed in the abstract) are not established there; even convergence of the iteration at $q=1$ relies on the Krasnoselskii–Mann relaxation without proof or rate in the paper (plain successive approximations oscillate). The omitted hypothesis $q<1$ is exactly what the conclusion needs.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis $q<1$ to Proposition prop:added-1 and either (a) add a contained convergence/rate analysis of the Krasnoselskii–Mann iteration for the $q=1$ affine disc BIE (restoring an explicit FNN error bound for the Poisson case), or (b) restrict the explicit-error-bound claims (abstract, Theorem error-bounds-thrm's final clause, Section 6.1.4 narrative) to $\lambda>0$.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised explicit FNN/PFNN error bounds (and any convergence rate for the boundary-function iteration) are unsupported for the Poisson forward problem, the paper's primary example, and for the abstract's blanket 'explicit error bounds' claim. Theorem error-bounds-thrm's own inequalities remain valid for Helmholtz-type problems with $\lambda>0$ (where $q<1$), and the semi-linear recurrence uses such sub-problems, so those parts survive.
issues.title: FNN error bound is undefined/vacuous at q=1, the regime of the Poisson BIE
issues.why_classification: The stated bound is undefined exactly at the non-expansiveness constant attained by the paper's main Poisson example, so a central advertised guarantee is missing there; restoring it requires a new (though contained) analysis or excluding a main example from the theory's coverage — more than a routine local fix, but avoiding new global proof architecture or major loss since the Helmholtz and semi-linear cases remain covered.

Step 4 evaluates the PFNN (hence this volume-potential quadrature) at exactly the same polar grid points $(r_i,\theta_j)$ that serve as quadrature nodes in Step 2, so the sum contains the term $\Phi(x,x)\psi_n(x)$, which is undefined ($-\infty$). Unlike the linear Poisson/Helmholtz implementations, where the singularity is explicitly handled by adaptive quadrature, the RPFNN rule specifies no treatment, so the algorithm is ill-defined at every grid evaluation point, and the $D_2$-type discretization error entering the error bounds invoked in Lemma lem:added-1 is not controlled by the stated rule.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Notice that we can decompose the error into a component arising from the fixed point iterations and another due to the neural network approximation by writing $\left\|\tilde{u}_n - u \right\|_{\Omega} \leq \left\|\tilde{u}_n - u_n \right\|_{\Omega} + \left\|u_n - u \right\|_{\Omega}$.
Step 1. Construct the PDE (\ref{iteration}) with source term $\psi_n(x) := -\lambda u_n(x) + F(x,u_n(x))$.

where $\epsilon_{\Omega}^{RPFNN}, \epsilon_{\partial \Omega}^{RPFNN}$ denote the errors associated with the PFNN construction in the domain and on the boundary, as given by (\ref{error-domain}) and (\ref{error-boundary}) respectively.

issues.failure_explanation: In the RPFNN, the sub-PDE solved at step $n$ has source $\psi_n$ built from the latest approximate iterate $\tilde u_{n-1}$; its exact solution is $T(\tilde u_{n-1})$, not $T(u_{n-1})=u_n$. Hence $\|\tilde u_n-u_n\| \le q\|\tilde u_{n-1}-u_{n-1}\|+\epsilon^{RPFNN}$, so by induction $\|\tilde u_n-u_n\|\le\epsilon^{RPFNN}(1-q^n)/(1-q)$, which can be arbitrarily larger than the one-step error $\epsilon^{RPFNN}$ (e.g., $q$ close to 1 with fixed per-step error gives limiting error $\approx\epsilon/(1-q)$). The proof's implicit step $\|\tilde u_n-u_n\|\le\epsilon^{RPFNN}$ is therefore invalid, and the stated interior bound in (error-recurrent) is false in general. (The boundary bound is not affected in the same way, since the boundary condition is re-imposed at each step.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the invalid step with the standard perturbed-contraction recursion $\|\tilde u_n-u_n\|\le q\|\tilde u_{n-1}-u_{n-1}\|+\epsilon^{RPFNN}$, yielding the corrected bound $\|\tilde u_n-u\|_{\Omega}\le\frac{\epsilon^{RPFNN}_{\Omega}}{1-q}+q^n\|u_0-u\|_{\Omega}$ (the boundary bound needs no accumulation term).
issues.overall_effect: The stated RPFNN interior error guarantee of Lemma lem:added-1 is false as written: per-iteration PFNN errors enter the next source term and accumulate with amplification $1/(1-q)$; the error-propagation narrative built on (error-recurrent) in Section 6.1.4 is likewise unreliable in its quantitative form.
issues.title: RPFNN error bound omits accumulation of per-step PFNN errors
issues.why_classification: The stated guarantee is false and the repair, while contained and standard, necessarily changes the stated bound (an amplification factor $1/(1-q)$ appears) and requires replacing the proof's key step — a limited weakening leaving a recognizably comparable result, but more than a routine local fix.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims the Helmholtz BIE kernel is weakly singular, in contrast to the Poisson case. In fact, from the paper's own correct starting formula, using $K_0'=-K_1$ and $y_1(y_1-x_1)+y_2(y_2-x_2)=|x-y|^2/2$ on the unit circle, the kernel is $\frac{\sqrt{\lambda}|x-y|K_1(\sqrt{\lambda}|x-y|)}{4\pi}$ — bounded, with a removable singularity and limit $1/(4\pi)$, exactly as in the Poisson case (a limit the paper itself derives two displays later, contradicting the claim). The displayed closed form is also wrong: it has an erroneous $|x-y|^2$ in the denominator (should be $|x-y|$) and an extra factor $1/|x-y|$ in the final simplification, producing a non-integrable $1/|x-y|^2$-type expression that motivated the false singularity claim.
